Model the vintage robbie the banker coin bank toy using the reference image

Reference files (read them, don't modify them), in ./references/:
- ./references/robie.jpg

Make it in Blender, working in the current directory.
- A Blender 5 instance is running for you with no window (background mode). Use it through the `blender`
  MCP tools: run Python (`bpy`) with execute_blender_code, and look things up with the API and manual
  search tools. Blender's working directory is the current directory. The scene starts as Blender's
  default one (a cube, a camera and a light).
- There is no window to screenshot. To check your work, render it to an image file and look at the image
  (render_thumbnail_to_path, render_viewport_to_path, or a render of the scene camera to a file).
  Keep renders quick: a single tool call may take at most 5 minutes.
- Build it in Blender itself; don't write the model or the images any other way.
- Save the finished result in ./output/ (only what is in ./output/ is published):
  - the model or scene as one .glb file (glTF binary), shown on the site in an interactive 3D viewer:
    `bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath=..., export_format='GLB')`, without Draco or meshopt
    compression, at most 15 MB;
  - one or more final renders as .png or .jpg, at most 2 MB each, from camera angles you choose.
  At most 8 files in all.
- Tools available on this machine: python3 3.15.0 (standard library only), node 26.12.0 (no npm packages), ffmpeg 9.0.2, ffprobe 9.0.2. Don't install packages or download anything (no asset
  libraries or add-ons).
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you made.

Read image file `./references/robie.jpg` as model-visible image output.

import bpy, math
from mathutils import Vector

# clear
bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
bpy.ops.object.delete(use_global=False)
for coll in [bpy.data.meshes, bpy.data.curves, bpy.data.cameras, bpy.data.lights]:
    pass

# materials
def make_mat(name, color, rough=0.3, metallic=0.0):
    m=bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes=True
    bsdf=m.node_tree.nodes["Principled BSDF"]
    bsdf.inputs["Base Color"].default_value=(*color,1)
    bsdf.inputs["Roughness"].default_value=rough
    bsdf.inputs["Metallic"].default_value=metallic
    # clearcoat-ish via specular
    try: bsdf.inputs["Specular IOR Level"].default_value=0.6
    except: pass
    return m

YELLOW=make_mat("YellowPlastic",(1.0,0.78,0.05),0.22)
YELLOW2=make_mat("YellowDark",(0.95,0.70,0.02),0.28)
BLACK=make_mat("BlackPlastic",(0.02,0.02,0.02),0.35)
BLACK_GLOSS=make_mat("BlackGloss",(0.01,0.01,0.01),0.15)
WHITE=make_mat("WhitePlastic",(0.95,0.95,0.93),0.25)
GREY=make_mat("EyeWhite",(0.92,0.90,0.85),0.2)
DARKBROWN=make_mat("DarkBrown",(0.08,0.05,0.03),0.4)

def assign(obj, mat):
    if obj.data and hasattr(obj.data,'materials'):
        obj.data.materials.append(mat)

def cyl(name, loc, radius, depth, mat, rot=(0,0,0), radius_top=None):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(vertices=64, radius=radius, depth=depth, location=loc, rotation=rot)
    o=bpy.context.active_object; o.name=name; assign(o,mat)
    # bevel modifier for soft edges
    mod=o.modifiers.new("bev","BEVEL"); mod.width=0.03; mod.segments=3
    bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()
    return o

def sphere(name, loc, scale, mat, rot=(0,0,0)):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_uv_sphere_add(segments=48, ring_count=32, location=loc, rotation=rot)
    o=bpy.context.active_object; o.name=name; o.scale=scale; assign(o,mat)
    bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()
    return o

def box(name, loc, scale, mat, rot=(0,0,0)):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(location=loc, rotation=rot)
    o=bpy.context.active_object; o.name=name; o.scale=scale; assign(o,mat)
    mod=o.modifiers.new("bev","BEVEL"); mod.width=0.02; mod.segments=2
    return o

def torus(name, loc, major, minor, mat, rot=(0,0,0)):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=major, minor_radius=minor, major_segments=48, minor_segments=16, location=loc, rotation=rot)
    o=bpy.context.active_object; o.name=name; assign(o,mat); bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()
    return o

# --- BODY ---
# black base
cyl("BaseBlack",(0,0,0.14),1.03,0.16,BLACK_GLOSS)
# lower body main - slightly tapered via cone? use cylinder then scale top?
body=cyl("Body",(0,0,0.78),1.0,1.05,YELLOW)
# make top slightly narrower: can't taper cylinder primitive easily, use cone truncated
# Replace with cone approach: delete and use primitive_cone
bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
body.select_set(True); bpy.ops.object.delete()
bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(vertices=64, radius1=1.02, radius2=0.94, depth=1.05, location=(0,0,0.78))
body=bpy.context.active_object; body.name="Body"; assign(body,YELLOW)
mod=body.modifiers.new("bev","BEVEL"); mod.width=0.04; mod.segments=3; bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()

# front seam (thin dark line)
box("BodySeam",(0,-0.965,0.78),(0.008,0.01,0.5),BLACK)

# gap ring between body and head (black)
cyl("NeckGap",(0,0,1.36),0.92,0.09,BLACK)

# HEAD
bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(vertices=64, radius1=0.94, radius2=0.97, depth=0.78, location=(0,0,1.79))
head=bpy.context.active_object; head.name="Head"; assign(head,YELLOW)
mod=head.modifiers.new("bev","BEVEL"); mod.width=0.05; mod.segments=3; bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()

# top black disc
cyl("TopDisc",(0,0,2.19),0.86,0.05,BLACK_GLOSS)
# top disc grooves (3 thin lines at back part) - small boxes on top
for i in range(4):
    box(f"TopGroove{i}",(-0.0,0.35+i*0.09,2.22),(0.55,0.015,0.008),BLACK)
# Actually grooves should be subtle dark lines - already black disc, use yellow? skip color diff: use slightly grey
# keep

# coin slot on back of head
box("CoinSlot",(0,0.96,1.95),(0.14,0.02,0.025),BLACK, rot=(0,0,0))

# --- EYES ---
for sx, name in [(-0.34,"L"),(0.34,"R")]:
    # socket ring (dark brown torus facing forward -Y)
    torus(f"EyeRing{name}",(sx,-0.88,1.92),0.20,0.035,DARKBROWN, rot=(0,0,0))
    # eyeball white sphere flattened
    sphere(f"Eyeball{name}",(sx,-0.90,1.92),(0.19,0.10,0.19),GREY)
    # pupil black lower part: sphere cut - use sphere offset down-front
    sphere(f"Pupil{name}",(sx,-0.975,1.80),(0.11,0.05,0.09),BLACK_GLOSS)

# small teeth under head front
for sx in [-0.12,0.12]:
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(vertices=16, radius1=0.045, radius2=0.0, depth=0.12, location=(sx,-0.82,1.32), rotation=(math.radians(180),0,0))
    o=bpy.context.active_object; o.name="Tooth"; assign(o,WHITE)

# --- SHOULDERS ---
for sx, name in [(-1.0,"L"),(1.0,"R")]:
    # axis along X: rotate cylinder Z by 90deg around Y
    cyl(f"Shoulder{name}",(sx,0,1.05),0.30,0.28,YELLOW, rot=(0,math.radians(90),0))

# --- FEET ---
for sx, name, ang in [(-0.92,"L", math.radians(18)),(0.92,"R", math.radians(-18))]:
    # sole black
    fsole=sphere(f"FootSole{name}",(sx,-0.62,0.13),(0.34,0.68,0.14),BLACK_GLOSS, rot=(0,0,ang))
    # foot yellow teardrop: sphere scaled, pointed front: use cone+sphere combo - sphere scaled
    foot=sphere(f"Foot{name}",(sx,-0.62,0.22),(0.32,0.64,0.20),YELLOW, rot=(0,0,ang))
    # taper front: add cone? keep sphere, add groove rings: two thin torus scaled around foot near front
    # grooves: thin black/yellow-dark lines - use torus scaled
    for gi, gy in enumerate([-0.95,-1.02]):
        t=torus(f"FootGroove{name}{gi}",(sx*0.92,gy,0.24),0.18,0.012,YELLOW2, rot=(math.radians(90),0,ang))
        t.scale=(1,1,1.6)

# --- ARMS via curves ---
def make_arm(name, points):
    cu=bpy.data.curves.new(name,'CURVE'); cu.dimensions='3D'; cu.bevel_depth=0.075; cu.bevel_resolution=4; cu.resolution_u=12
    sp=cu.splines.new('BEZIER'); sp.bezier_points.add(len(points)-1)
    for i,p in enumerate(points):
        bp=sp.bezier_points[i]; bp.co=p; bp.handle_left_type='AUTO'; bp.handle_right_type='AUTO'
    ob=bpy.data.objects.new(name,cu); bpy.context.collection.objects.link(ob); assign(ob,BLACK_GLOSS)
    return ob

# robot right arm (viewer left, x=-) goes down then forward curl
make_arm("ArmR",[(-1.12,0,0.95),(-1.22,-0.15,0.65),(-1.18,-0.45,0.42),(-1.05,-0.68,0.38)])
# claw C shape: torus partial - use torus and delete? approximate with torus rotated
claw=torus("ClawR",(-0.92,-0.78,0.38),0.16,0.055,BLACK_GLOSS, rot=(math.radians(90),0,math.radians(20)))
# robot left arm (viewer right, x=+) goes forward to tray
make_arm("ArmL",[(1.12,0,0.95),(1.30,-0.25,0.70),(1.22,-0.65,0.62),(0.95,-0.95,0.72)])

# --- TRAY (held in left hand, front right) ---
# tray disc flattened
tray=cyl("Tray",(0.62,-1.12,0.78),0.38,0.05,BLACK_GLOSS, rot=(0,0,0))
tray.scale=(1,1.15,1)
# small tab pointing left-down
box("TrayTab",(0.22,-0.92,0.78),(0.12,0.09,0.025),BLACK_GLOSS, rot=(0,0,math.radians(-30)))
# white ring on tray
torus("TrayRing",(0.62,-1.12,0.815),0.26,0.015,WHITE, rot=(0,0,0))

result={"ok":True, "objects":[o.name for o in bpy.data.objects]}

import bpy, math

def make_mat(name, color, rough=0.3):
    if name in bpy.data.materials: return bpy.data.materials[name]
    m=bpy.data.materials.new(name); m.use_nodes=True
    m.node_tree.nodes["Principled BSDF"].inputs["Base Color"].default_value=(*color,1)
    m.node_tree.nodes["Principled BSDF"].inputs["Roughness"].default_value=rough
    return m

BLACK=bpy.data.materials["BlackPlastic"]
WHITE=bpy.data.materials["WhitePlastic"]

def add_text(name, body, loc, rot, size, mat, align='CENTER'):
    cu=bpy.data.curves.new(name,'FONT'); cu.body=body; cu.size=size; cu.align_x=align; cu.align_y='CENTER'
    cu.extrude=0.008; cu.bevel_depth=0.002
    ob=bpy.data.objects.new(name,cu); bpy.context.collection.objects.link(ob)
    ob.location=loc; ob.rotation_euler=rot
    if mat: cu.materials.append(mat)
    return ob

# ROBIE on front chest - facing -Y
t=add_text("TextROBIE","ROBIE",(0,-0.99,1.08),(math.radians(90),0,math.radians(180)),0.22,BLACK)
t.scale=(1.15,1,1)

# $ on tray - facing up (+Z), tray top z ~0.815
add_text("TextDollarTray","$",(0.62,-1.12,0.82),(0,0,math.radians(180)),0.38,WHITE)
# $ small? also white ring already

# Top disc text - facing up, readable from front (-Y side reading)
# rotate so text reads when viewed from front above: rotation Z 180 maybe
add_text("TextTop1","Radio Shack",(0,0.08,2.225),(0,0,math.radians(180)),0.16,WHITE)
add_text("TextTop2","ROBOTIC BANKER",(0,0.28,2.225),(0,0,math.radians(180)),0.075,WHITE)

Modeled the vintage Robie the Banker (Radio Shack Robotic Banker) coin bank in Blender from the 4-view reference.

The model captures the bright yellow two-part cylindrical body and head with black separator gap and base, black top disc with "Radio Shack / ROBOTIC BANKER" lettering and groove lines, large round white eyes with dark rims and low black pupils, small white teeth under the head, rear coin slot, yellow shoulder discs with black curved arms — a C-claw on one side and a black coin tray with white ring and "$" on the other — oversized yellow teardrop feet with black soles, and bold black "ROBIE" chest lettering, all in glossy plastic materials.

Saved in `./output/`:
- `robie_the_banker.glb` (1.9 MB, uncompressed glTF binary)
- `robie_hero.png` — front 3/4 hero view
- `robie_front.png` — straight front view
- `robie_back_top.png` — back/top view showing coin slot and top disc
